key_insight: The paper shows that deep generative models with piecewise-affine decoders and Gaussian mixture priors can be identified in an unsupervised setting by breaking algebraic symmetries rather than relying on classical ICA assumptions.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled route to recover latent structure and decoder behavior in nonlinear generative models, even when the decoder is discontinuous or non-injective.
method: Use domain contrast to eliminate mixture-label symmetries in the latent GMM.
Use mechanism contrast to ensure each decoder branch is uniquely exposed by a boundary.
Use interaction contrast to prevent latent-component/decoder-branch parameter conspiracies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical identifiability hierarchy—law, map, posterior, and pointwise identifiability—derived from assumptions on the data-generating process rather than learning procedure.
watch_item: The strongest guarantees depend on algebraic symmetry conditions and interaction contrast, so practical verification of these assumptions in real data may be difficult.
paper_title: Beyond ICA: Identifiability by Symmetry Breaking
